title: Living with Chick Webb and Trueheart
summary: Chick Webb took him under his wing, in rooms across from the Bandbox shared with guitarist Trueheart.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, what were you thinking of a guy like Chick, like that? That was terrific, wasn't it?
Oh, yeah. So --
That was --
I moved in with him.
Well, when did you first hear him play some drums?
Not until we got the job at the Savoy. I think it was about a week later.
Well, that must have thrilled you when you heard him play drums, didn't it?
Yeah. Well, no instrument thrilled me but the trumpet.
Oh, Cootie, honestly? No kidding.
I don't think so. Not doing that era. Nothing thrilled me but the trumpet.
Well, I'll be darned. Well, were you a few years younger than Chick?
Yeah.
So he was really taking you under his wing?
Yeah.
What kind of a place was he living in?
He was living right across the street from the Bandbox.
Oh, he was. What'd he have, one room?
Yeah. He had one room. And his guitar player used to live there.
Trueheart.
Trueheart.
He had another room. Trueheart had another room?
Yeah. Trueheart had another room, and I was living with Trueheart.
Oh, I see. And Chick was paying both rents.
Yeah. He wasn't paying but one rent.
Oh, yeah. I see.
And Ginger. He was a musician.
Who?
What was his name? Ginger. I don't know his last name.
No, I don't either.
Was he a piano player? I don't remember.
Yeah.
So he had the house. He had the apartment.
Oh, I see. So you were renting from him.
No, I wasn't renting from nobody.
No, but they were renting from him.
Yeah.
Yeah.
So --
So did you have any cash on you at all?
No.
Nothing.
Didn't have nothing.
But Chick wanted you to blow with the band?
Yeah. So --
Did you rehearse all the time? Did you get your horn out and blow all the time in the house?
Yeah. It was a In the musicians' house. There wasn't nobody staying there but musicians.
No kidding.
